A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Hilbert-guided local attention work despite the shortened title. Their complete main texts, figures, tables, equation, and appendices support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original attention runtime and memory benchmarks, ImageNet-1K accuracy, model throughput, and hardware and parameter studies in Section 4 and Appendices A.1–A.4.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100 accuracy and measurements using additional attention kernels.

M1.justification: Hilbert reordering, HWA/HSA/HNA attention patterns, shifted windows, global relative position bias, and HWT/HNT designs remain unchanged. The added kernel implementations execute existing attention patterns; the expanded caching description clarifies an existing component.

E1.justification: Table 5 in v2 adds classification on 32×32 CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100, extending the retained ImageNet evaluation within natural-image classification. Detection, segmentation, and generation are mentioned only as future applications.

E2.justification: The kernel comparison sets expand substantially across window and sliding attention. Tables 1 and 3 and Appendices A.1–A.2 add WSA/SA using xFormers, HWA/HSA using xFormers, and HSA using FlashAttention-2. Existing dense, FlexAttention, NATTEN, and SDPA comparisons remain.

E3.justification: The new CIFAR experiments introduce three-stage configurations with depths [2,6,4], head counts [3,6,12], patch size 2, and 300 training epochs, with corresponding window/neighborhood sizes documented in Table 5. Existing ImageNet and attention-benchmark protocols are unchanged.

E4.justification: The block-size study, batch/head sensitivity analyses, input-processing breakdowns, cross-hardware evaluations, and SDPA study are retained unchanged. The new backend comparison rows and CIFAR scores do not introduce a distinct ablation, robustness test, or error analysis.

E5.justification: Both versions specify timing averages over 10 runs of 100 iterations, with 25% warm-up and 75% measurement. No new seed information, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty-reporting procedures appear.

E6.justification: v2 adds substantial runtime/memory result blocks for additional kernels and a new classification table. CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100 accuracies are 92.2%/76.4% for HWT and 94.1%/79.9% for HNT. Table 3 additionally reports HSA (FA2) forward/backward times of 0.25/0.75 ms at 56×56 with a 7×7 kernel. Matched original table values and reported plots remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The runtime approximation in Equation 1 and the attention/block definitions are unchanged. The new notation for the cached path P(H,W) restates the existing mapping; no substantive derivation, assumption, theorem, or proof is added.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the same Hilbert-guided sparsity and efficiency claims, including approximately 4× window-attention and 18× slide-attention speedups and end-to-end acceleration with minimal accuracy loss. New experiments support these retained claims.

C2.justification: Section 4.2 adds explanations linking xFormers performance to element-wise sparse versus fused block-diagonal execution, and HSA compatibility to specialized banded kernels. It also explicitly identifies downstream detection, segmentation, and generation evaluations as future work.

D1.justification: v2 clarifies that Hilbert paths are computed and cached at model initialization, describes execution paths for the added kernels, and supplies CIFAR model and training configurations. The code link was already present in v1; its footnote and Appendix A.5 appearances do not establish newly available resources.

R1.justification: The reference list contains the same works, and the related-work discussion retains its positioning relative to local attention and optimized kernels. Citation-format corrections and additional experiments using already discussed libraries do not redefine the claimed novelty.

P1.justification: v2 shortens the title, updates author/header text and citation formatting, expands several implementation and interpretation passages, and adds brief code and language-model-use appendix sections. The principal section structure and most prose remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds the CIFAR table, expands existing efficiency tables, and adds traversal arrows to Figure 3. Several displays move, including v1 Table 8 becoming the expanded v2 Table 11. Conference headers and author layout change, while the remaining figure graphics are retained.

improvement.justification: The added xFormers/FlashAttention-2 measurements and CIFAR experiments provide useful additional evidence for kernel compatibility and accuracy retention. Clearer caching and configuration descriptions also help reproducibility. These strengthen the paper incrementally while preserving its method and principal ImageNet and end-to-end results.
